The templates should be updated to the latest 5.x so newly scaffolded apps get the current Bootstrap CSS/JS and its bug/security fixes.\\n\\n### Where it is pinned\\n\\n- `src/ProjectTemplates/Web.ProjectTemplates/package.json` pins `\\u0026#34;bootstrap\\u0026#34;: \\u0026#34;^5.3.3\\u0026#34;`.\\n- The vendored copies live under each template\\u0026#39;s `wwwroot/lib/bootstrap/dist/` (for example `content/BlazorWeb-CSharp/BlazorWebCSharp.1/wwwroot/lib/bootstrap/dist/`), which currently carry the 5.3.3 build (the `bootstrap.min.css` banner reads `Bootstrap v5.3.3`).\\n\\n### Expected\\n\\n`dotnet new` web templates (Razor Pages, MVC, Blazor Web, etc.) ship the latest Bootstrap 5.x (currently 5.3.8), with the vendored `dist` assets and their subresource-integrity hashes regenerated to match.\\n\\n### Actual\\n\\nTemplates ship Bootstrap 5.3.3.\\n\\n### How this was found\\n\\nAn end-to-end validation harness that scaffolds real templates from nightly builds asserts the shipped Bootstrap version against the latest upstream 5.x (via the npm registry) and verifies every subresource-integrity hash on the page matches the served bytes. The version assertion currently fails:\\n\\n```\\nBootstrap is behind: shipped 5.3.3, expected 5.3.8.\\nExpected: \\u0026#34;5.3.8\\u0026#34;\\nBut was:  \\u0026#34;5.3.3\\u0026#34;\\n```\\n\\n### Notes\\n\\n- Latest upstream: https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/releases/tag/v5.3.8\\n- When updating, regenerate the SRI `integrity` attributes referenced from the template layouts so they match the new asset bytes.\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67666\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"javiercn\",\"id\":6995051,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/javiercn\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/6995051?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\",\"feature-templates\",\"area-ui-rendering\"],\"comments\":1,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-07-08T09:24:43Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-26T08:21:45Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Bug\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

Is there an existing issue for this?\\n\\n- [X] I have searched the existing issues\\n\\n### Describe the bug\\n\\nIn the original ASP.Net Core/Angular templates, proxying was done in the back-end, while in the newer templates, the proxying moved to the client side.\\nThis new approach breaks the back-end Authentication middleware, since redirect requests for the authentication layer don\\u0026#39;t get redirected to the ASP.Net Core backend, but to the Angular client server, which results in CORS errors due to the client proxy not introducing CORS headers, like was possible with the previous template.\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThere should be a straight-forward, documented means to use Authentication middleware in ASP.Net Core with the new client-side proxy The page is in the template, but the Razor pages aren\\u0026#39;t loaded unless you choose to enable the individual auth or do it manually. It was previously working because Razor pages was loaded through `AddMvc()`, but since 3.x, the template only use `AddControllersWithViews()`.\\n\\nThe problem is not visible in Development environment, which use the `UseDeveloperExceptionPage()`, but only for `UseExceptionHandler(\\u0026#34;/Error\\u0026#34;)`, because the route doesn\\u0026#39;t exists, then the default route fallback provided by `UseSpa` takes over and returns an HTTP 200 with the default page as content.\\n\\n### To Reproduce\\n`dotnet new react`\\nedit `WeatherForecastController.cs` and throw an exception in the `Get()` method\\n`dotnet run` then go the the \\u0026#34;Fetch data\\u0026#34; page\\nyou should see the HTTP 500 request in your browser debugger for `https://localhost:5001/weatherforecast`\\n`dotnet publish` to build the react project\\nedit `launchSettings.json` and set `Production` as environment\\n`dotnet run` then go the the \\u0026#34;Fetch data\\u0026#34; page\\nyou should see the HTTP 200 request in your browser debugger for `https://localhost:5001/weatherforecast`\\n\\n### Proposals\\n\\nRemove the `#if (IndividualLocalAuth)` statements in `src/ProjectTemplates/Web.Spa.ProjectTemplates/content/Angular-CSharp/Startup.cs` around `services.AddRazorPages();` and `endpoints.MapRazorPages();`\\n\\nOr\\n\\nRemove the error page and `app.UseExceptionHandler(\\u0026#34;/Error\\u0026#34;);`. I don\\u0026#39;t find this page relevant for the SPA templates, the errors must be handled by the SPA itself.\\n\\n### Further technical details\\n- ASP.NET Core 3.1\\n\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/25661\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"mereth\",\"id\":2607099,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/mereth\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/2607099?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"bug\",\"investigate\",\"feature-spa\",\"affected-few\",\"severity-minor\",\"area-ui-rendering\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":4,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2020-09-06T18:58:22Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-05-01T21:20:50Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Bug\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

a package with static web assets.\\n  * Create a razor class library.\\n  * Add a wwwroot folder to it.\\n  * Add a javascript file under the wwwroot folder and have it do something simple like `console.log`\\n  * Run dotnet pack.\\n  * Open the generated package.\\n  * Validate that there are 4 folders:\\n    * build containing two props files\\n    * buildMultitargeting containing one props file.\\n    * buildTransitive containing one props file.\\n    * staticwebassets containing the javascript file that you added.\\n  * Validate that there are no additional folders like content or contentFiles\\n* Referencing a class library with static web assets.\\n  * Create a razor pages application\\n  * Reference the class library in the previous step by adding a project reference.\\n  * Go to index.cshtml and add a script tag with src `_content/\\u0026lt;\\u0026gt;/\\u0026lt;\\u0026gt;`\\n  * Run the application and validate that a message is logged into the console.\\n* Referencing a package with static web assets.\\n  * Create a second class library project.\\n  * Add a wwwroot folder\\n  * Add a javascript file under wwwroot and have it do something simple like `console.log`\\n  * Have the first class library reference this library as a package.\\n  * Add an entry to restore sources in the main app pointing to the location where the package for this library get generated.\\n  * Run pack on this class library.\\n  * Add a script tag for the javascript file in this library on the main app.\\n  * Build and run the application, validate that the two messages show up in the console.\\n* Publishing an app that references static web assets.\\n  * Publish the existing app.\\n  * Go to the publish folder.\\n  * Validate that there is a _content folder under wwwroot\\n  * Validate that it contains one subfolder for each of the class libraries.\\n  * Validate that the right javascript file is in each of the subfolders.\\n  * Validate that the files are not safeoutputs.description: WRITE-ONCE: do NOT call this tool with empty or placeholder arguments to probe or discover its schema — the required `body` field is listed in this schema; if you are not ready to post a real comment, call `noop` instead. Adds a comment to an existing GitHub issue, pull request, or discussion. Use this to provide feedback, answer questions, or add information to an existing conversation. For creating new items, use create_issue, create_discussion, or create_pull_request instead. IMPORTANT: Comments are subject to validation constraints enforced by the MCP server - maximum 65536 characters for the complete comment (including footer which is added automatically), 10 mentions (@username), and 50 links. Exceeding these limits will result in an immediate error with specific guidance. NOTE: Discussion comments are disabled for this workflow because discussions:write permission is not available. Set 'discussions: true' in the workflow's safe-outputs.add-comment configuration to enable discussion comments and request this permission. CONSTRAINTS: Maximum 1 comment(s) can be added. Target: *. This tool records a real comment intent. Do not use it for placeholder comments, auth checks, or probing. Call it only when the final comment body is ready; otherwise use noop or report_incomplete.
safeoutputs.name: add_comment

safeoutputs.description: Add labels to an existing GitHub issue or pull request for categorization and filtering. Labels must already exist in the repository. For creating new issues with labels, use create_issue with the labels property instead. CONSTRAINTS: Maximum 3 label(s) can be added. Only these labels are allowed: ["area-auth" "area-blazor" "area-commandlinetools" "area-dataprotection" "area-grpc" "area-healthchecks" "area-hosting" "area-identity" "area-infrastructure" "area-middleware" "area-minimal" "area-mvc" "area-networking" "area-perf" "area-routing" "area-security" "area-signalr" "area-ui-rendering" "area-unified-build" "by-design" "question" "external" "docs" "api-proposal" "test-failure" "performance"]. INTENT ENCOURAGED: Include rationale (string, max 280 chars) and confidence (exactly one of: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH) with each call. These fields are optional but strongly encouraged — they improve transparency and should normally be included. Use suggest: true alongside rationale and confidence to route for human review.
safeoutputs.name: add_labels

safeoutputs.description: Remove labels from an existing GitHub issue or pull request. Silently skips labels that don't exist on the item. Use this to clean up labels or manage label lifecycles (e.g., removing 'needs-review' after review is complete). CONSTRAINTS: Maximum 1 label(s) can be removed. Only these labels can be removed: [needs-area-label].
safeoutputs.name: remove_labels

safeoutputs.description: Report that a tool or capability needed to complete the task is not available, or share any information you deem important about missing functionality or limitations. Use this when you cannot accomplish what was requested because the required functionality is missing or access is restricted. When a bash command is blocked by security policy, call this tool with reason set to "security".
safeoutputs.name: missing_tool

safeoutputs.description: Log a transparency message when no significant actions are needed. Use this to confirm workflow completion and provide visibility when analysis is complete but no changes or outputs are required (e.g., 'No issues found', 'All checks passed'). This ensures the workflow produces human-visible output even when no other actions are taken.
safeoutputs.name: noop

safeoutputs.description: Set the type of a GitHub issue. Pass an empty string "" to clear the issue type. Issue types must be configured in the repository or organization settings before they can be assigned. INTENT ENCOURAGED: Include rationale (string, max 280 chars) and confidence (exactly one of: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH) with each call. These fields are optional but strongly encouraged — they improve transparency and should normally be included. Use suggest: true alongside rationale and confidence to route for human review.
safeoutputs.name: set_issue_type

safeoutputs.description: Report that data or information needed to complete the task is not available. Use this when you cannot accomplish what was requested because required data, context, or information is missing.
safeoutputs.name: missing_data

safeoutputs.description: Signal that the task could not be completed due to an infrastructure or tool failure (e.g., MCP server crash, missing authentication, inaccessible repository). Use this when required tools or data are unavailable and the task cannot be meaningfully performed. This is distinct from noop (no action needed) — it indicates an active failure that prevented the task from running. Provide a specific reason and optional details so downstream issue aggregation can preserve complete incomplete-signal context. The workflow framework will treat this as a failure signal even when the agent exits successfully.
safeoutputs.name: report_incomplete
